Put the targets on an isolated 192.0.2.0/24 training segment and snapshot them first. The controller can enumerate only the assigned lab addresses, request each device’s unauthenticated information page, and retain the model and firmware banner. For a deliberately vulnerable training image, test a short list of seeded default credentials against the lab login endpoint and stop after the first successful session rather than brute-forcing. When a session is established, send a benign administrative action such as changing the simulated status LED, rotating the training password, or adding a marker to the device event log. Discovery records address, port, and banner. Authentication records whether the seeded account is accepted and immediately timestamps the result. Control submits one fixed JSON action and verifies the expected mock response. Cleanup logs out, restores the snapshot, and deletes the session token. Keep the target image’s API paths and credentials unique to the exercise instead of copying a real manufacturer’s interface. A simple request sequence is a GET to the lab status path, a POST to the lab login path with the seeded account, a POST to the lab command path with an action value of set-training-led, and a final POST to logout. Add assertions that reject any address outside the training subnet and fail closed if DNS, a default route, or a non-lab certificate appears. During the run, capture the requests and have trainees map each one to a mitigation: remove default credentials, require mutually authenticated administration, patch the firmware, restrict management to a maintenance VLAN, and alert on unusual administrative commands. At the end, destroy the containers or reflash the devices from known-good images. The same sequence can be rerun after remediation to demonstrate that discovery may remain visible while authentication and control fail. The lab boundary and benign action make the demonstration measurable, but the controller still models a real exploit chain and should remain private to the assessment team.
